Emergency room co-payment</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>A $50 emergency room co-payment applies to each hospital emergency room visit. The emergency room co-payment does not apply if the patient: a) Is admitted to the hospital immediately following such treatment. b) Is treated in the emergency room for 12 or more hours. c) Dies in the emergency room. This emergency room co-payment does not apply toward the individual deductible, family deductible, or out-of-pocket expense limits.</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>A $50 emergency room co-payment applies to each hospital emergency room visit. If the patient is admitted to the hospital immediately following such treatment, the emergency room co-payment does not apply. (Other reasons for waiver of the co-payment vary by plan.) This emergency room co-payment does not apply toward the individual deductible, family deductible or co-payment provisions.</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>2. Office visit co-payment</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>A $15 co-payment applies to each covered outpatient visit to a network physician (except for preventive care, smoking cessation, mental health, and substance abuse services).</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>A $10 co-payment applies to each covered office visit to a network provider.</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>3. Retail Pharmacy</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Covered prescriptions or refills are subject to the deductibles.
